title: DBK and KSystemInformer: two published caller-trust boundaries
summary: A source-level comparison of Cheat Engine privilege checks and System Informer verified-client policy, with package identities and x64dbg’s separate user-mode role. No driver is declared vulnerable simply because it exposes powerful research features.
author: Observatory editorial
takeaways: DBK’s visible CREATE path requires SeDebugPrivilege and has additional compile-time-gated checks.
KSystemInformer documents signing and client-state restrictions, including consequences of unsigned modules and tampering.
An INF’s file names and service settings are packaging evidence—not proof of a release signature or matching binary hash.
x64dbg is a separate user-mode debugger, not a substitute name for a kernel driver.
